interpretation_boundary: This confirms or weakens reversible null-conserving spatial phase-separation claims only.

questions.1_large_domains: Yes: all 4/4 Stage 7B winner seeds retained both large dispersion and at least twofold finite-domain growth; the median final scale ratio was 16.1118. The stricter sustained-coarsening count was 0/4 because the late slope was negative.
questions.2_pure_rotation: Pure rotation counts were 0/8 and 0/4; equal-explanation status at 4096² was False.
questions.3_unusual_vs_matched: Winner final-dispersion rank was 2/9 against the eight Stage 7A matched controls and 2/5 against the four Stage 7B controls, because matched_00 had still greater coarse dispersion. However, the winner's median final finite-domain scale ratio was 16.1118 while every Stage 7B matched-control median was below 1. The winner was unusual in domain growth but not uniquely largest in coarse dispersion. Strict classification is D: The winner did not reproduce the full sustained-coarsening criterion in at least three of four Stage 7B seeds.
questions.4_rotation_oscillator: Yes, largely: Stage 7B median late lag-4/8 recurrence was 0.977148/0.984118 for the winner and 1/1 for pure rotation. Recurrence shared with rotation is scaffold-inherited, not an independent signature of organization.
questions.5_genuine_coarsening: Early-to-mid-time growth was reproducible and strong (median peak scale ratio 98.4459), but it was not sustained: the scale relaxed to a median 16.1118 times initial and every Stage 7B winner late-half slope was negative. This supports domain formation followed by saturation/relaxation, not unbounded or sustained late-time coarsening.
questions.6_reversible_occupancy_creation: The Stage 7B winner median occupied-fraction change was 0.050987 while every charge audit stayed exact, and the discovery run reversed byte-for-byte. The observations are consistent with reversible balanced occupancy creation, but this campaign does not identify a unique causal fraction.
questions.7_beyond_phase_separation: No. There is no lineage, heredity, reproduction, adaptive fitness, or organism test.

stage_a_gate.classification_reason: The winner passed the continuation gate, but its position within the matched-rule distribution was mixed rather than clearly exceptional or generic.
